skill.name: spawn-parallel
skill.description: Coordinate independent AI subagent tasks with clear boundaries, outputs, and recovery guidance.
skill.summary: Coordinate multiple independent AI subagents in parallel with explicit ownership and validation steps.

content.value_statement: Large AI tasks slow down when independent work is handled one step at a time. This skill helps teams split safe parallel work into bounded subagent tasks with clear outputs.
actual_capabilities: Defines criteria for deciding whether tasks are independent.
Shows a compact context contract for each subagent task.
Demonstrates spawning multiple Task calls in one response.
Lists custom dotagent agent roles for exploration, implementation, verification, and testing.
Provides retry, context enhancement, scope reduction, and escalation guidance.
Includes examples for parallel explorers and mixed implementation tasks.
limitations: It does not execute agents by itself.
It assumes Task tool support and custom dotagent agent names.
It does not automatically prevent shared file conflicts.
It references an error-recovery skill that is not included in this package.

use_cases.title: Split implementation work
use_cases.description: Break independent coding tasks into bounded agent assignments with explicit file ownership.

use_cases.title: Run parallel verification
use_cases.description: Assign separate agents to inspect tests, behavior, and integration risks after a change.

use_cases.title: Design repeatable agent workflows
use_cases.description: Create a clear pattern for launching, collecting, and validating multi-agent results.

prompt_templates.title: Find independent tasks
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a small change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the spawn-parallel pattern to identify which parts of this request can run independently. List each task, its inputs, and any file conflicts.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare parallel contexts
prompt_templates.prompt: Create focused subagent contexts for these independent tasks. Include the task goal, relevant files, ownership boundaries, read-only references, and expected output.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a mixed-agent batch
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow using different agent roles.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a parallel batch that uses explorer, implementer, verifier, and tester roles where appropriate. Explain why each task is independent and how results should be validated.

prompt_templates.title: Review a failed parallel run
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these parallel task results and apply the failure-handling rules. Recommend retry, context enhancement, scope reduction, escalation, or abort for each failed task.

output_examples.input: I need authentication, API routes, and database models explored before implementation.
output: Three explorer tasks are proposed because each area can be read independently.
Each task receives only the relevant file set and returns compact findings.
The final step is to collect all results before planning implementation.

output_examples.input: One implementation agent failed because the database connection pattern was unclear.
output: The recommended recovery is context enhancement with the missing configuration and connection references.
The retry should keep the original task goal and request the same output destination.
Repeated failures should move to scope reduction or escalation.

output_examples.input: Two agents may need to edit related service files at the same time.
output: The plan separates ownership so each agent writes to a distinct file area.
Shared interfaces are treated as read-only references unless a contract owner is assigned.
Validation checks confirm outputs exist and match the agreed format.

best_practices: Define file ownership before launching parallel agents.
Give each agent only the context needed for its task.
Validate every output before combining results.
anti_patterns: Do not parallelize tasks that depend on each other.
Do not let multiple agents edit the same file without a contract.
Do not retry failed tasks without adding useful context or reducing scope.

faq.question: What does this skill help coordinate?
faq.answer: It helps coordinate multiple independent AI subagents that can work at the same time.

faq.question: Does it run commands or scripts?
faq.answer: No. It is guidance for using the Task tool and does not include executable scripts.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: When should I avoid this pattern?
faq.answer: Avoid it when tasks share mutable files, depend on each other, or need one result before another starts.

faq.question: How does it reduce conflicts?
faq.answer: It asks you to define owned files, read-only references, and contracts for shared interfaces.

faq.question: How are failed tasks handled?
faq.answer: The skill recommends retry, context enhancement, scope reduction, escalation, or abort based on the failure type.
